In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the velocity dispersion profile of NGC 1399 is consistent with a mass-to-light ratio that increases with radius and is in agreement with that expected for the presence of a central supermassive black hole.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the velocity dispersion of the metal-rich cluster system in the Fornax galaxy NGC 13999 is consistent with the value expected for a dark matter halo of mass M ~ 1012 M⊙, which is in turn consistent with the value of M derived from X-ray observations.
NGC 1399 has a mass within a radius of about 50 kpc of 1.5 × 1014M⊙, a mass-to-light ratio of 50–130, a mean metallicity of about 1/3 of the solar value, and a mean age of 10 Gyr.
, within the errors, our velocity dispersion is consistent with that measured in other galaxies of the same luminosity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the velocity dispersion of the globular cluster population in NGC 1399 is significantly lower than that of its underlying stellar population.
the radial velocity distribution of globular clusters in the field of NGC 1399 does not show any sign of rotation.
the radial velocity dispersion of NGC 1399 is not significantly affected by the presence of a large number of metal-poor globular clusters.
